content_units: Family Game Night Fit

For 6 adults and 2 teenagers, the sweet spot is   easy-to-teach, low-conflict games with quick turns   and either   6–8 player support   or strong team/party play. The picks below stay within roughly   30–75 minutes  , avoid harsh elimination, and work well when attention spans and experience levels are mixed.
10 Board Games That Work Well
Game   Player Count   Typical Duration   Complexity   Why it suits a mixed-age group
Just One   3–7   20–30 min   Very light   Fully cooperative word-guessing game; easy for teens and adults to enjoy together, with no conflict at all.
Codenames   4–8+   30 min   Light   Team-based word association keeps everyone involved and works especially well with 8 players split into teams.
Dixit Odyssey   3–12   30–45 min   Light   Creative clue-giving and beautiful art make it accessible even for non-gamers; scoring is gentle and social.
Ticket to Ride   2–5   45–60 min   Light-medium   Simple route-building with minimal confrontation; great if you split into smaller tables or rotate groups.
Sushi Go Party!   2–8   20–40 min   Light   Simultaneous card drafting keeps turns fast and fun; cute theme helps mixed ages engage quickly.
Wavelength   2–12   30–45 min   Very light   Team-based discussion game that sparks laughter and conversation rather than competition.
Camel Up   3–8   30–45 min   Light   Silly camel-racing bets create excitement without direct attacks or elimination.
Herd Mentality   4–20   20–30 min   Very light   Players try to match the majority, which makes it welcoming for casual players and teens alike.
So Clover!   3–6   30 min   Light   Cooperative word-association puzzle that feels clever without being difficult or confrontational.
Concept   4–12   30–40 min   Light   Guessing words through icons is intuitive, low-pressure, and inclusive across ages and gaming experience.
Best Picks for Your Exact Group of 8
Option 1:   Codenames     Best overall for exactly 8 players in teams   Social, low-conflict, easy to replay
View Game
Option 2:   Camel Up     Best board-game feel for 6–8 players   Fast, funny, and spectator-friendly
View Game
Option 3:   Dixit Odyssey     Best for creative mixed-age play   Gentle scoring, strong visual appeal
View Game
Option 4:   Wavelength     Best if you want lots of laughter and conversation   Team-based and very easy to teach
View Game
Smooth Setup for the Evening
- Start with   Herd Mentality  ,   Just One  , or   Wavelength   to warm everyone up.
- Move to   Camel Up   or   Dixit Odyssey   for the main game slot.
- Keep   Sushi Go Party!   ready as a fast closer or second round.
- If you want everyone playing together the whole time, prioritize   Codenames, Camel Up, Wavelength, Herd Mentality, Dixit Odyssey,   and   Concept  .
